why: The doc sentence is verbatim (changelog.md:19, one-sentence bullet under 2.1.219, nothing reversing it; corroborated by settings.md:431). The identifier absence is also real: 0 hits for strictAllowlist across packages/apps TS with grep -a, and SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS at packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182 is exactly ['deniedDomains','allowedDomains','allowManagedDomainsOnly']. But BOTH halves of the claimed consequence are false, measured. (1) 'silently dropped' is wrong on both parse paths. Ran the real parser (parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1 with {network:{allowedDomains:['github.com'],strictAllowlist:true}}): the STRICT path used by user/project/local settings THROWS 'invalid sandbox network setting: strictAllowlist' (networkSection, :249) - loud, not silent; the TOLERANT managed path records an explicit drop {path:'sandbox.network.strictAllowlist', reason:'invalid sandbox network setting: strictAllowlist', action:'stripped'} (toleratedNetworkSection, :341-345). Whether the desktop shell surfaces managed drops at all is inert-worklist section 3 item 4, a dated owner decision about ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, not this key. (2) 'the prompt path stays reachable' is false because there is no per-host egress prompt path for sandboxed commands in this fork to stay reachable. resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement (:900) reduces the whole sandbox network block to one bit, egress:'open'|'denied', and the module documents why at :846-873 (NO_DOMAIN_FILTER): Seatbelt rejects any host but * or localhost, unshare/firejail toggle the whole namespace, the Windows profile has one network.enabled boolean - 'on every backend we have, outbound network is one bit. The per-domain layer is the egress proxy (R19), deliberately parked.' With no allow/deny/PROMPT egress decision, strictAllowlist has no prompt to convert into a deny; adding a parser key would create a setting that binds nothing, which is exactly what the module's 'unenforceable' diagnostics and IsolationNetworkPostureV1 (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:50-67) exist to prevent. Sibling-subsystem trap: the only network-domain prompt in the fork is the Bash tool's curl/wget domain check (pre-tool-use.ts:1985-1997 + permission-manager.ts:475 isDomainWhitelisted), a permission-mode prompt in the tool pipeline that reads nothing from sandbox.network.* - and settings.md:431 scopes strictAllowlist to sandboxed commands only, so it would not gate that prompt even if implemented. Finally, this is not an unnoticed gap: parity-audit row 8 (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690) records R19 as PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 ('nuzhno vsyo razreshit, ogranicheniya budut potom'), with egress deliberately OPENED by d214cb63 and the plan retained; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md already names strictAllowlist in its precedence chain (:53), its user/managed/CLI-only layer rule (:26, :55) and its failing-test list (:57, :98). The cited file:line is that plan's Global Constraints bullet, i.e. the finding's own evidence is the tracked plan for it. It also duplicates the better-worded phase1 sweep row under the sandboxing slug (data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:395), whose ourState correctly stops at 'no reader'.
correctedState: sandbox.network.strictAllowlist has no reader: SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182) accepts only deniedDomains, allowedDomains and allowManagedDomainsOnly. It is NOT silently dropped - a user/project/local settings file carrying it is rejected outright with 'invalid sandbox network setting: strictAllowlist' (:249), and a managed policy carrying it records an explicit stripped-key drop (:341-345). And there is no prompt for it to suppress: resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement (:900) collapses the sandbox network block to egress 'open'|'denied' because no isolation backend we ship can filter by domain (:846-873), so the fork has no per-host egress allow/deny/prompt decision at all. The per-domain layer, including strictAllowlist's documented semantics and its user/managed/CLI-only layer rule, is R19 - PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 (parity audit row 8) with the plan retained at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md. The one residual worth noting is separate from the claim: rejecting the key at strict scope means a conforming Claude user-settings file with strictAllowlist fails to load its sandbox block, which contradicts this module's own 'a conforming settings file must be ACCEPTED' rule (:133-135).
